summary: This work designs a two-layer superconducting architecture implementing all five universal continuous-variable gates (rotation, displacement, squeezing, Kerr, and beam splitter) using a DC-SQUID mode, a fluxonium qubit for nonlinear interactions, and two ancillary qubits. Numerical simulations achieve fidelities $\geq 98\%$ across all gates within state-of-the-art parameter regimes, with gate times ranging from 33 ns (displacement) to 228 µs (Kerr at $\mathcal{F} = 98.8\%$).
motivation: Superconducting platforms currently lack scalable architectures for universal continuous-variable quantum computation, with existing approaches limited by geometric constraints in planar resonator designs or incomplete gate sets.
method: The circuit employs a DC-SQUID encoded as the CV mode ($\omega_m = 10$ GHz) with a fluxonium qubit ($\omega_f = 400$ MHz, $\alpha_f/2\pi \gtrsim 500$ MHz) coupled via tunable quadratic coupling $g_{m,f}(\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}})$, and two capacitively coupled auxiliary qubits ($g_{m,i} \approx 104$–105 MHz) for Gaussian operations. Parameters are tuned via external pulses and detunings to realize each gate; fidelities are evaluated on coherent states with $\nu = 2$ (mean photon number $\bar{n} = 4$).
result: Rotation and beam splitter gates achieve $\geq 99\%$ fidelity; displacement is near-perfect; squeezing reaches $\mathcal{F} = 99.8\%$ with $\tau_s = 205$ ns at $g_0 = 8.3$ MHz, $\Omega_S = 150$ MHz; Kerr reaches $\mathcal{F} = 98.8\%$ with $\tau_k \approx 228$ µs at $g_{m,f} \approx 0.83$ MHz—all within demonstrated superconducting coherence times ($T_1, T_2 \gg 100$ µs).
